DataType.description:
An abstract data type.

- `number` includes int, bigint, float, decimal, double, real, etc.
- `string` includes char, varchar, text, etc.
- `timestamp_tz` timezone-aware
- `timestamp_naive` without timezone
- `date` the calendar date portion of a timestamp; always without a timezone
- `boolean`
- `null`
- `other`
DataType.title: DataType

Dimension.description:
A dimension represents a selectable column expression.

These can be physical columns, complex SQL snippets, or formulas.

id.description:
The unique identifier for this dimension.
This identifier is used as its reference and must be unique across all dimensions, measures, and relations in this model. Changing this identifier may invalidate existing references.

type.description: The abstract data type of this dimension.

expr_sql.description:
A sql select column expression that produces a scalar for each row. This is often a column name.
One of `expr_sql` or `expr_calc` can be provided. If neither is provided, defaults to `expr_sql` being the `id` of this dimension.
expr_sql.title: Expr Sql

expr_calc.description: A [Hex calc formula](https://learn.hex.tech/docs/explore-data/cells/calculations) which produces a scalar for each row.
expr_calc.title: Expr Calc

unique.description:
If true, this dimension is unique for all rows in this model.
This dimension may be used in the construction of primary keys.
unique.title: Unique

name.description:
The user-facing display name for this dimension.
If omitted, defaults to the sentence-case value of `id`.
name.title: Name

description.description: The user-facing description of this dimension.
description.title: Description

Dimension.title: Dimension

EntityId.description:
All IDs must conform to the following rules:

- Begins with a lowercase letter or an underscore
- Only contains lowercase letters, underscores, and numbers
- Between 2 and 128 characters long (inclusive)

In addition, the following IDs are reserved by the system and cannot be used:
dataset, model, this, self, env or any ID beginning with '__hex'.
EntityId.title: EntityId

Measure.description: A measure represents a aggregated expression.

id.description:
The unique identifier for this measure.
This identifier is used as its reference and must be unique across all measures in this model. Changing this identifier may invalidate existing references.

func.description:
A standard aggregation function to use.
One of `func`+`of`, `func_sql` or `func_calc` must be provided.

of.description:
Specifies the dimension over which the `func` aggregation is applied.
This dimension can be specified as a referenced dimension ID, or an inline dimension. If `type` is unspecified in an inline dimension, it is assumed to be `number`.
of.title: Of

func_sql.description: An aggregating sql select expression that produces a scalar over a set of rows.
func_sql.title: Func Sql

func_calc.description: An aggregating [Hex calc formula](https://learn.hex.tech/docs/explore-data/cells/calculations) which produces a scalar over a set of rows.
func_calc.title: Func Calc

type.description:
The abstract data type of this measure.
If omitted, defaults to `number`.

filters.description:
A list of boolean dimensions which must be true for a row to be included in the measure's aggregation.
Only supported for `func` measures.
These dimensions can be specified as a referenced dimension ID, or an inline dimension. If `type` is unspecified in an inline dimension, it is assumed to be `boolean`.
filters.title: Filters

name.description:
The user-facing display name for this measure.
If omitted, defaults to the sentence-case value of `id`.
name.title: Name

description.description: The user-facing description of this measure.
description.title: Description

semi_additive.description:
Semi-additive aggregation that selects specific rows before calculation.
Filters to minimum or maximum values of the specified dimension, then aggregates only those rows.

Measure.title: Measure

base_sql_query.description:

Relation.description:
A relation defines a link between two models, aka a "join".

The properties of a relation can be referenced with dot-syntax within a
bracket reference, such as `${relation_id.dimension_id}`.

id.description:
The unique identifier for this relation.
Typically, this should be the id of the model being joined to.
Relations with the same id will be considered symmetric with one another.
Relation ids must be unique across all dimensions, measures, and relations in this model. Changing this identifier may invalidate existing references.

target.description:
The identifier of the target model for this relation.
If omitted, defaults to the value of `id`.

type.description:
The cardinality of the join, from the base model to the target.
This is declared to ensure Hex can properly invoke fan-out prevention.

join_sql.description:
The SQL condition to join the base model to a target.
Within this snippet, all dimensions and relations (including this one) are in scope for `${ }` interpolation.
join_sql.title: Join Sql

SemiAdditive.description:
A semi-additive specification controls how measures aggregate over specific
dimensions.

Semi-additive measures are useful for metrics like account balances or inventory
levels, where you want the most recent value within each group rather than
summing all values.

over.description:
List of dimensions that determine row selection for aggregation.
Rows will be filtered to those with minimum or maximum values of these dimensions.
Limited to a single dimension.
over.title: SemiAdditiveOver

groupings.description:
List of dimension identifiers to group by when determining min/max values.
The semi-additive filtering will be applied within each group.
groupings.title: SemiAdditiveGroupings

SemiAdditive.title: SemiAdditive

SemiAdditiveOverMember.description:
A criteria for determining the rows to include in the semi-additive measure.

Defines which dimension to use for row selection and how to select the rows.

dimension.description: The identifier of the dimension to use for row selection.
dimension.title: Dimension

pick.description:
Whether to select rows with the minimum or maximum dimension value.
If omitted, defaults to 'max'.
pick.title: Pick

SemiAdditiveOverMember.title: SemiAdditiveOverMember

View.description:
A semantic view represents a curated set of model properties and join paths.

Views can be used to define a fit-for-purpose exposure of models and their
properties, providing a cleaner sandbox for users and agents interacting with
your semantic project.

This identifier is used as its reference and must be unique across all views in the project. Changing this identifier may invalidate existing references.

base.description: The ID of the model that this view is based on.

name.description:
The user-facing display name for this view.
If omitted, defaults to the sentence-case value of `id`.
name.title: Name

description.description: The user-facing description of this view.

Visibility.description:
The visibility determines the scope the associated declaration.
Either `public`, `internal`, or `private`.

`visibility` is not to be relied on as a security control and is only used
to visually hide content in the UI. For the strongest security guarantees,
configure OAuth or role-based access within your database.
